lesson.menu_title: The Other Side of the Argument
lesson.menu_desc: Reading an analyst note with two sides and summarizing both with although, whereas, despite and however -- 30 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 16 -- The Other Side of the Argument
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Marcio Ferreira Santos | Lesson 16 -- The Other Side of the Argument

listenings.text: Good morning. You asked me for both sides of the private label plan, so here they are. The case for it is margin. Our own brands make about eight points more margin than the national brands, whereas the price for the customer is around twenty percent lower. That is a good deal for both sides. However, there are two problems. The first is cannibalization. Although the private label grows, part of that growth comes from our own national brands, not from the competitors. The second is the suppliers. Despite our good relationship, two big suppliers have already said that they will reduce their promotions with us if we give their space to our own brands. I concede that this is a real risk. But on balance, I would still move forward, slowly, in three categories first, with a clear review after six months.

In a visa interview, the officer may push back on your reason for the trip. A common version is this: you can take an online course from Brazil, so why do you need to travel? Do not get defensive, and do not argue. The best answer has two parts. First, concede the point. Yes, online courses exist, and some of them are good. Then give the counterargument in one short sentence: although the content is online, the case discussions happen in the classroom, with executives from other countries. That is the part you cannot download. Notice the order. You start with what is true in the officer's argument, and only then do you say why your choice is still right. It sounds calm, it sounds honest, and it shows that you have thought about the question before.

extra_audio.text: First, she states the question in one sentence. Then she gives the bull case. After that, she gives the bear case. Next, she adds a caveat about her own data. Finally, she gives her view on balance.

reading.rtitle: Cash-and-Carry Retail — Two Sides of the Loyalty Price
paras: Our view on the company is neutral, and this note sets out both sides. The company plans to move part of its promotions from broad price cuts to loyalty prices in its app. Although the change is small today, it could shape margins for the next three years.

The bull case is simple. Loyalty prices cost far less margin than broad cuts, and the company gets data on every customer who uses them. Whereas a broad cut goes to everybody, a loyalty price goes only to the customers who need a reason to come back. If app use doubles, the margin gain could offset the higher technology costs within a year.

The bear case is about reach. Despite strong growth, the app still reaches only a third of customers, and many of them are older shoppers who prefer cash and paper flyers. However, the bigger risk is the competition. If a main competitor answers with a broad price cut, customers may simply change stores, and the company would have to cut prices as well.

We concede that the bear case is valid in the short term. One caveat on our own numbers: they come from a test in only two regions. On balance, we think the strategy is right, but we expect the first two quarters to be difficult.

gist.prompt: Read once for the main idea. What is the main message of the note?
choices: The strategy is a mistake, and the company should go back to broad price cuts in every store as soon as possible
The strategy has real risks, but on balance the analyst thinks it is right
The app already reaches most of the customers

items: A loyalty price goes to every customer.
Whereas a broad cut goes to everybody, a loyalty price goes only to the customers who need a reason to come back.
According to the note, the bigger risk is the competition.
The third paragraph says: however, the bigger risk is the competition.
The analyst's numbers come from all the regions.
One caveat: they come from a test in only two regions.
The analyst expects the first two quarters to be difficult.
The last sentence says the first two quarters will be difficult.
